Hi Tom —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the forecast. I put together two concise commercial paths and attached the pricing workbook (obs_pricing_breakdown.xlsx) plus a draft SOW (Acea_Observability_SOW_v2.pdf) so your procurement/legal team can see the exact language we expect on surge/commit. High-level:

Option A — Committed Slab + Seats (recommended for predictable spend)
- Retention: 30/90/365 tiers priced per GB-month; slab committed at 90-day equivalent with overage at 120% of marginal rate.
- Tracing: Included up to a per-month span cap; additional full-span ingest billed per million spans.
- Dashboards: Seat-based pricing for editors (full access) + project add-on for cross-team views.
- Surge handling: 10% monthly buffer included; additional burst is charged but we offer a 1-month smoothing credit if quarterly usage spike is >2x baseline.

Option B — Metered (pay-as-you-go with smoothing)
- Retention: Metered per GB-month; no slab commitment.
- Tracing: Metered; sampling policies configurable to avoid over-ingestion.
- Dashboards: Same seat model but billed monthly with no upfront commit.
- Surge handling: We offer a transient smoothing policy: first two bursts per year (defined as >150% of baseline for 48+ hrs) are discounted at 50% of marginal rate, subsequent bursts billed normally.

Commercial delta: Option A gives roughly 18–25% unit cost savings vs Option B at your forecasted 12-month consumption; the attached workbook shows the math across three retention horizons and two tracing intensities.

If procurement prefers a guaranteed smoothing instead of ad hoc discounts, we can propose a 12-month concession (month-of-burst credit pool) in the SOW; Ben is on copy to confirm commercial flexibility and Irene to confirm SOW language.

Next steps: choose Option A or B, confirm any target discount (we can run a concession model), and we’ll issue a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Cheers,

Looping in briefly with the commercial posture we should take. Priya laid out solid options. Two proposals from my side for procurement to consider:

1) Intro concession: 15% off year-one unit rates for Option A if Acea commits to a 12-month slab at 90-day retention for traces and enables our prefix/KV caching on two high-traffic endpoints. In return we put the smoothing clause in the SOW: a 20% credit pool applied to the month after a documented burst.

2) Flexible pilot: No commit (Option B) but a 6-month pilot with capped exposure: we apply a $25k surge cushion (non-recurring credit) to be used for bursts and revisit pricing at pilot end.

Irene — legal note: if we do a credit pool, SOW needs clear definition of burst triggers and reconciliation cadence. Also confirm seats vs seats-with-readonly distinction so procurement knows what consumes seat licenses.

Priya — happy to sign off on these if Acea prefers a conservative runway. Tom — if procurement wants to move quickly, option 1 gives predictable economics and an easier path to a renewal with increased retention.
